ei.subject: 공통영어1
ei.title: A Better Future for Coffee Waste / Become a Mushroom Farmer

fullPassage:
The famous German musician Johann Sebastian Bach once said, "Without my morning coffee, I'm just like a dried-up piece of goat." Today this sentiment is shared by many, with coffee shops springing up on almost every street corner, and it is common to see city residents walking around with a cup of coffee in hand. According to the International Coffee Organization (ICO), approximately 10 million tons of coffee was consumed worldwide between 2020 and 2021, and Koreans made a significant contribution to this huge total, consuming 150,780 tons of coffee. This means that every Korean adult drank an average of one cup of coffee every day throughout the year. Clearly, for Koreans and other world citizens, coffee is not just a drink but a daily necessity.

How much of a coffee bean is used to make coffee?
The world's widespread love of coffee comes at a substantial environmental cost, as the extraction process generates significant waste. Only 0.2 percent of a coffee bean is used to make coffee, with the remaining 99.8 percent disposed of as waste. As a result, the vast quantity of coffee consumed worldwide produces millions of tons of coffee waste each year.
So, what happens to all the waste from the coffee extraction process? Spent coffee grounds (SCGs) are classified as general waste and sent to landfills. There they break down, releasing methane, a greenhouse gas that is approximately 25 times more potent than CO₂. Some SCGs are incinerated instead of being buried, but this releases a lot of CO₂: 338 kg per ton. However, neither of these waste management options takes into account the potential value of coffee grounds. Although the grounds contain valuable organic compounds and minerals, they are simply destroyed.

Fortunately, thanks to increased awareness of the coffee waste problem, companies, organizations, and governments around the world are working hard to improve the environmental impact of the coffee industry through circular economy measures. A circular economy promotes the reuse of resources for as long as possible, reducing waste and environmental costs.

An example of a circular economy in action occurs when a chain of coffee shops collaborates with an organization to collect spent coffee grounds from its shops. These grounds are processed to remove impurities and dried out. The resulting SCGs are sold to fertilizer companies, where they are transformed into organic fertilizer. This fertilizer is later sold back to the coffee shop chain. The chain provides the fertilizer to local eco-friendly farmers, who then sell their produce back to the chain. The farm produce can be used to create various food items, such as rice chips and dried sweet potatoes, which are sold in the chain's coffee shops. By repurposing coffee grounds in this manner, related businesses and local farmers can benefit both economically and environmentally.

Recycled coffee grounds have a wide range of uses, including coffee logs, fabrics for clothing and shoes, and reusable cups. Coffee logs, for instance, generate more heat and burn for a longer time than wood. Fabric made from coffee grounds absorbs sweat, dries quickly, and provides UV protection. Reusable cups from coffee grounds not only have a visually appealing appearance but also preserve the taste of the coffee.

Korea has shown a growing interest in recycling spent coffee grounds in recent years. The government is taking steps toward the creation of a sustainable recycling system in the coffee industry, while companies are dedicating themselves to researching and developing new uses for coffee waste. By recycling materials such as coffee waste, individuals can also help protect the environment. With continued efforts, the recycling of used coffee grounds is expected to increase, encouraging more sustainable methods of enjoying coffee for years to come.

Did you know that you can grow tasty mushrooms right in your home using spent coffee grounds? Coffee grounds contain the perfect nutrients for growing mushrooms. Here is a step-by-step guide to help you get started. First, mix 80 percent coffee grounds with 20 percent mushroom spawn. Then, thoroughly wash a milk container and make four small holes in the sides. Fill the container about two-thirds full of the mixture and close it tightly. Next, find a warm and dark place with a temperature between 18 and 25°C, and place the container there for two to four weeks until the mixture turns completely white. When this happens, move the container to a bright area with indirect sunlight and cut the top off. To keep the mixture from drying out, spray it with water twice a day. Within a week, you will notice tiny mushrooms emerging. When the mushrooms grow tall, they are ready to be picked. After that, you can enjoy your mushrooms with your favorite dish!

questions.passage: The world's widespread love of coffee comes at a (A)[substantial / marginal] environmental cost, as the extraction process generates (B)[significant / insignificant] waste. Only 0.2 percent of a coffee bean is used to make coffee, with the remaining 99.8 percent (C)[disposed / composed] of as waste. As a result, the vast quantity of coffee consumed worldwide produces millions of tons of coffee waste each year.
questions.stem: (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 커피에 대한 전 세계적 사랑은 상당한(substantial) 환경 비용을 수반하며, 추출 과정에서 상당한(significant) 폐기물이 발생합니다. 나머지 99.8%는 폐기물로 처리됩니다(disposed).
det.analysis:
✅ ① substantial–significant–disposed: 99.8%가 폐기물이므로 환경 비용이 상당하고(substantial), 폐기물도 상당하며(significant), disposed of가 원문
❌ ② insignificant는 99.8% 폐기와 모순
❌ ③ marginal(미미한)은 substantial의 반의어로 부적합
❌ ④ 전부 부적합
det.tip: substantial(상당한) ↔ marginal(미미한) / disposed of(처리되다) vs composed of(구성되다)

questions.passage: Fortunately, thanks to increased (A)[awareness / ignorance] of the coffee waste problem, companies, organizations, and governments around the world are working hard to improve the environmental impact of the coffee industry through (B)[circular / linear] economy measures. A circular economy (C)[promotes / restricts] the reuse of resources for as long as possible, reducing waste and environmental costs.
questions.stem: (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 커피 폐기물 문제에 대한 인식(awareness) 증가 덕분에, 순환(circular) 경제 조치를 통해 개선하고 있습니다. 순환 경제는 자원의 재사용을 촉진합니다(promotes).
det.analysis:
✅ ③ awareness–circular–promotes: 모두 원문 그대로 적합
❌ ① restricts는 promotes의 반의어로 순환경제 취지에 모순
❌ ② ignorance(무지)는 awareness 반의어, linear(선형)은 circular 반의어
❌ ④ ignorance와 restricts 둘 다 부적합
det.tip: awareness(인식) ↔ ignorance(무지) / circular economy(순환경제) = 재사용 촉진

questions.passage: These grounds are processed to remove (A)[impurities / nutrients] and dried out. The resulting SCGs are sold to fertilizer companies, where they are (B)[transformed / converted] into organic fertilizer. This fertilizer is later sold back to the coffee shop chain. The chain provides the fertilizer to local eco-friendly farmers, who then sell their produce back to the chain. By (C)[repurposing / recycling] coffee grounds in this manner, related businesses and local farmers can benefit both economically and environmentally.
questions.stem: (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 불순물(impurities)을 제거하고 건조합니다. 유기 비료로 변환됩니다(transformed). 커피 찌꺼기를 재활용(repurposing)함으로써 혜택을 받습니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① impurities–transformed–repurposing: 원문 기준 모두 적합
❌ ② converted는 transformed와 유사하나 원문은 transformed, recycling은 repurposing과 다름
❌ ③ nutrients(영양분)는 remove와 결합 시 부적합
❌ ④ nutrients와 converted 둘 다 원문과 불일치
det.tip: impurities(불순물) ↔ nutrients(영양분) / transformed into(~으로 변환되다) / repurposing(재활용) ≈ recycling이지만 원문 기준

questions.passage: Spent coffee grounds (SCGs) are classified as general waste and sent to ①<u>landfills</u>. There they break down, releasing methane, a greenhouse gas that is approximately 25 times more ②<u>potent</u> than CO₂. However, neither of these waste management options takes into account the ③<u>potential</u> value of coffee grounds. Although the grounds contain valuable organic compounds and minerals, they are simply ④<u>preserved</u>.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ①매립지에 보내집니다. ②25배 더 강력한. ③잠재적 가치. 유기 화합물과 광물질이 있음에도 단순히 파괴됩니다(destroyed).
det.analysis:
✅ ④ preserved → destroyed: 귀중한 화합물과 광물이 있음에도 '보존'이 아니라 '파괴'되는 것이 원문
❌ ①②③: 원문 그대로 적절
det.tip: preserved(보존되다) ↔ destroyed(파괴되다) / Although가 역접 단서 → 가치가 있는데도 파괴됨

questions.passage: Coffee logs, for instance, generate more heat and burn for a longer time than wood. Fabric made from coffee grounds ①<u>repels</u> sweat, dries quickly, and provides UV protection. Reusable cups from coffee grounds not only have a ②<u>visually</u> appealing appearance but also ③<u>preserve</u> the taste of the coffee. Korea has shown a ④<u>growing</u> interest in recycling spent coffee grounds in recent years.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 커피 찌꺼기로 만든 원단은 땀을 흡수하고(absorbs) 빨리 마릅니다. ②시각적으로 매력적인. ③커피 맛을 보존합니다. ④재활용에 대한 관심이 증가하고 있습니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① repels → absorbs: 원단이 땀을 '튕기는' 것이 아니라 '흡수한다'가 원문
❌ ②③④: 원문 그대로 적절
det.tip: repels(튕기다/밀어내다) ↔ absorbs(흡수하다) / dries quickly는 흡수 후 빨리 마르는 기능

questions.passage: An example of a circular economy in action occurs when a chain of coffee shops ①<u>collaborates</u> with an organization to collect spent coffee grounds from its shops. The resulting SCGs are sold to fertilizer companies, where they are transformed into organic fertilizer. The chain provides the fertilizer to local ②<u>eco-friendly</u> farmers, who then sell their produce back to the chain. By repurposing coffee grounds in this manner, related businesses and local farmers can benefit both ③<u>individually</u> and environmentally. The government is taking steps toward the creation of a ④<u>sustainable</u> recycling system in the coffee industry.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ①커피 전문점 체인이 단체와 협력합니다. ②친환경 농부. 경제적으로(economically) 그리고 환경적으로 혜택을 받습니다. ④지속 가능한 재활용 시스템.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ individually → economically: 원문은 'economically and environmentally'이므로 individually 부적절
❌ ①②④: 원문 그대로 적절
det.tip: individually(개별적으로) ↔ economically(경제적으로) / benefit economically and environmentally = 경제적·환경적 혜택

questions.passage: Today this sentiment is shared by many, with coffee shops springing up on almost every street corner, and it is common to see city residents walking around with a cup of coffee in hand. According to the ICO, approximately 10 million tons of coffee was consumed worldwide between 2020 and 2021. This means that every Korean adult drank an average of one cup of coffee every day throughout the year. Clearly, for Koreans and other world citizens, coffee is not just a drink but a daily __________.
questions.stem: 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 커피숍이 거리마다 생기고, 한국인 성인이 매일 한 잔씩 마시므로 커피는 음료가 아니라 일상적 필수품(necessity)입니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② necessity: 'not just a drink but a daily ~'에서 음료 이상의 것 = 필수품
❌ ① luxury(사치품)는 매일 마시는 것과 모순
❌ ③ preference(선호)는 'a daily ~' 형태에 부적합
❌ ④ tradition(전통)은 문맥과 무관
det.tip: necessity(필수품) / not just A but B 구문: A 이상의 B

questions.passage: Spent coffee grounds (SCGs) are classified as general waste and sent to landfills. There they break down, releasing methane, a greenhouse gas that is approximately 25 times more potent than CO₂. Some SCGs are __________ instead of being buried, but this releases a lot of CO₂: 338 kg per ton. However, neither of these waste management options takes into account the potential value of coffee grounds.
questions.stem: 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 일부 SCG는 매립 대신 소각(incinerated)되지만, 이것은 많은 CO₂를 배출합니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① incinerated: 매립(buried) 대신 하는 것이며 CO₂를 338kg 배출 → 소각이 적합
❌ ② recycled(재활용)는 CO₂ 대량 배출과 모순
❌ ③ composted(퇴비화)는 CO₂ 338kg과 맞지 않음
❌ ④ exported(수출)는 문맥과 무관
det.tip: incinerate(소각하다) / instead of being buried가 핵심 단서 → 매립 아닌 또 다른 처리법

questions.passage: An example of a circular economy in action occurs when a chain of coffee shops collaborates with an organization to __________ spent coffee grounds from its shops. These grounds are processed to remove impurities and dried out. The resulting SCGs are sold to fertilizer companies, where they are transformed into organic fertilizer. This fertilizer is later sold back to the coffee shop chain.
questions.stem: 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 커피 전문점 체인이 단체와 협력하여 매장에서 사용한 커피 찌꺼기를 수거합니다(collect).
det.analysis:
✅ ③ collect: 매장에서 커피 찌꺼기를 모아서 처리하는 순환경제 과정
❌ ① generate(생성하다)는 from its shops와 부적합
❌ ② distribute(배포하다)는 수거의 반대 방향
❌ ④ consume(소비하다)는 찌꺼기를 소비한다는 것이 부자연스러움
det.tip: collect(수거하다) / collaborates with an organization이 수거 체계를 암시

questions.passage: The world's widespread love of coffee comes at a <u>substantial</u> environmental cost, as the extraction process generates significant waste. Only 0.2 percent of a coffee bean is used to make coffee, with the remaining 99.8 percent disposed of as waste.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 substantial과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 커피에 대한 전 세계적 사랑은 상당한(substantial) 환경 비용을 수반합니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ considerable: substantial = 상당한 = considerable
❌ ① minor(사소한)는 반의어
❌ ② artificial(인공적인)은 무관
❌ ③ marginal(미미한)은 반의어
det.tip: substantial ≈ considerable ≈ significant / ↔ minor, marginal, trivial

questions.passage: The government is taking steps toward the creation of a sustainable recycling system in the coffee industry, while companies are <u>dedicating</u> themselves to researching and developing new uses for coffee waste. By recycling materials such as coffee waste, individuals can also help protect the environment.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 dedicating과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 기업들은 커피 폐기물의 새로운 용도를 연구·개발하는 데 전념하고(dedicating) 있습니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① committing: dedicate oneself to ≈ commit oneself to (전념하다)
❌ ② surrendering(항복하다)은 전혀 다른 의미
❌ ③ withdrawing(철수하다)은 반의어
❌ ④ hesitating(주저하다)은 반의어
det.tip: dedicate ≈ commit ≈ devote (전념하다) / dedicate oneself to = ~에 전념하다

questions.passage: Spent coffee grounds (SCGs) are classified as general waste and sent to landfills. There they break down, releasing methane, a greenhouse gas that is approximately 25 times more <u>potent</u> than CO₂. Some SCGs are incinerated instead of being buried, but this releases a lot of CO₂.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 potent와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 메탄은 CO₂보다 약 25배 더 강력한(potent) 온실가스입니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② powerful: potent = 강력한 = powerful
❌ ① weak(약한)은 반의어
❌ ③ abundant(풍부한)은 양적 개념으로 다름
❌ ④ visible(눈에 보이는)은 무관
det.tip: potent ≈ powerful ≈ strong (강력한) / 온실가스 효과의 강도를 비교하는 맥락

questions.passage: Recycled coffee grounds have a <u>wide</u> range of uses, including coffee logs, fabrics for clothing and shoes, and reusable cups. Coffee logs, for instance, generate more heat and burn for a longer time than wood.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 wide와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 재활용된 커피 찌꺼기는 넓은(wide) 범위의 용도를 가지고 있습니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ limited: wide(넓은) ↔ limited(제한된)
❌ ① broad(넓은)는 동의어
❌ ② extensive(광범위한)는 동의어
❌ ④ diverse(다양한)는 유사 의미
det.tip: wide ≈ broad ≈ extensive / ↔ limited, narrow, restricted

questions.passage: The government is taking steps toward the creation of a <u>sustainable</u> recycling system in the coffee industry, while companies are dedicating themselves to researching and developing new uses for coffee waste. With continued efforts, the recycling of used coffee grounds is expected to increase.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 sustainable과 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 정부가 지속 가능한(sustainable) 재활용 시스템을 만들기 위해 노력하고 있습니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ temporary: sustainable(지속 가능한) ↔ temporary(일시적인)
❌ ① permanent(영구적인)는 유사 의미
❌ ② enduring(오래 견디는)는 유사 의미
❌ ③ lasting(지속되는)는 유사 의미
det.tip: sustainable ≈ lasting ≈ enduring / ↔ temporary, short-lived, unsustainable

questions.passage:
(A) The world's widespread love of coffee comes at a substantial environmental <u>cost</u>, as the extraction process generates significant waste.
(B) Recycled coffee grounds have a wide range of uses, including coffee <u>logs</u>, fabrics for clothing and shoes, and reusable cups. Coffee logs, for instance, generate more heat and burn for a longer time than wood.
questions.stem: (A)와 (B)의 밑줄 친 단어의 문맥적 의미로 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) 환경적 비용/대가(cost)를 수반합니다. (B) 커피 통나무(logs)는 더 많은 열을 발생시킵니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 비용/대가 – 나무 통나무: (A) cost = 비용/대가, (B) log = 나무(연료용 통나무)
❌ ① 원인은 cost의 의미가 아님
❌ ② 원인은 cost의 의미가 아님, 기록/로그는 IT용어
❌ ④ 비용/대가는 맞지만 기록/로그는 여기서 부적합
det.tip: cost: 비용/대가/희생 (at a cost = 대가로) / log: 통나무(연료), 기록(IT), 일지(항해)

questions.stem:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 단어로 적절한 것은?
"a substance added to soil to make plants grow more effectively"

det.korean: "식물이 더 효과적으로 자라도록 토양에 첨가하는 물질" = 비료(fertilizer)
det.analysis:
✅ ③ fertilizer: 식물 성장을 위해 토양에 추가하는 물질 = 비료
❌ ① extraction(추출)은 꺼내는 과정
❌ ② awareness(인식)는 물질이 아님
❌ ④ impurity(불순물)는 제거 대상
det.tip: fertilizer(비료) / organic fertilizer = 유기 비료

questions.passage: According to the International Coffee Organization (ICO), approximately 10 million tons of coffee was __________ (consume) worldwide between 2020 and 2021.
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: 약 1천만 톤의 커피가 전 세계적으로 소비되었습니다(consumed).
det.analysis:
✅ consumed: 수동태 was + p.p. 구조. coffee was consumed = 커피가 소비되었다
주어 coffee가 소비 '당하는' 대상이므로 수동태
det.tip: consume → consumed (수동태: was consumed) / consume-consumed-consumed

questions.passage: With continued efforts, the recycling of used coffee grounds is expected to increase, __________ (encourage) more sustainable methods of enjoying coffee for years to come.
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: 지속적인 노력으로 커피 찌꺼기 재활용이 증가할 것으로 예상되며, 더 지속 가능한 방법을 장려하면서(encouraging).
det.analysis:
✅ encouraging: 분사구문으로 동시동작 표현. 주절의 주어(recycling)가 encourage하는 것이므로 현재분사
수동이 아닌 능동 → encouraging
det.tip: 분사구문: 주어 동일 + 동시 동작 → V-ing / encourage → encouraging

ch: reducing the size of coffee beans
the reuse of resources for as long as possible
questions.passage: The world's widespread love of coffee comes at a substantial environmental cost, as the extraction process generates significant waste. Only 0.2 percent of a coffee bean is used to make coffee, with the remaining 99.8 percent disposed of as waste. Fortunately, thanks to increased awareness of the coffee waste problem, companies, organizations, and governments around the world are working hard to improve the environmental impact of the coffee industry through circular economy measures. A circular economy promotes __________, reducing waste and environmental costs. An example of a circular economy in action occurs when a chain of coffee shops collaborates with an organization to collect spent coffee grounds from its shops.
questions.stem: 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 순환 경제는 __________을(를) 촉진하여 폐기물과 환경 비용을 줄입니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ the reuse of resources for as long as possible: 순환경제의 핵심 = 자원 최대한 재사용
❌ ① 원자재 수출은 순환경제와 무관
❌ ② 생산량 증가는 폐기물 감소와 모순
❌ ③ 커피콩 크기 줄이기는 무관
det.tip: circular economy = 순환경제 → reuse(재사용)가 핵심 원리

questions.passage: The chain provides the fertilizer to local eco-friendly farmers, who then sell their produce back to the chain. The farm produce can be used to create various food items, such as rice chips and dried sweet potatoes, which are sold in the chain's coffee shops. By repurposing coffee grounds in this manner, related businesses and local farmers can benefit __________. The government is taking steps toward the creation of a sustainable recycling system in the coffee industry.

det.korean: 커피 찌꺼기를 이렇게 재활용함으로써 관련 기업과 지역 농부는 __________ 혜택을 받을 수 있습니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① both economically and environmentally: 경제적(판매/수익)+환경적(폐기물 재활용) 양면 이익
❌ ② only는 both와 모순
❌ ③ 정부 보조금은 본문에 언급 없음
❌ ④ 생산비용 절감만은 환경적 이점 누락
det.tip: benefit both A and B = A와 B 양쪽 혜택 / 순환경제의 이중 이점: 경제+환경
